facts.statement: Edgarosaurus is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur that contains only one known species, E. muddi.
facts.quote: Edgarosaurus is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur from the Thermopolis Shale, containing one species, E. muddi.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Edgarosaurus was discovered in the Shell Creek Member of the Thermopolis Shale in the spring of 1993.
facts.quote: The well-preserved holotype specimen of Edgarosaurus (MOR 751) was found in the Shell Creek Member, the uppermost of the three members of the Thermopolis Shale, during the spring of 1993.

facts.statement: The species Edgarosaurus muddi was named in 2002 by Pat S. Druckenmiller.
facts.quote: Edgarosaurus muddi was named in 2002 by Pat S. Druckenmiller.

facts.statement: The type specimen was found in Early Cretaceous (Albian, approximately 105 million years ago) rocks in Montana, United States.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo fue encontrado en las rocas del Cretácico inferior (Albiense, hace unos 105 millones de años) en el estado de Montana en los Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: During the Cretaceous, the location where Edgarosaurus fossils were found was covered by the shallow Western Interior Seaway known as the Niobrara Sea.
facts.quote: Durante el Cretácico, este lugar estaba recubierto por un mar interior somero denominado como el mar de Niobrara.

facts.statement: Druckenmiller estimated the total length of Edgarosaurus to be roughly 3.2 to 3.7 meters.
facts.quote: Druckenmiller estimated the total length of Edgarosaurus to be roughly 3.2 - 3.7 m, a figure derived from the proportions of Dolichorhynchops and Peloneustes.

facts.statement: The cranium of the holotype specimen of Edgarosaurus is 47.5 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The cranium of the holotype specimen of Edgarosaurus is 47.5 cm long.

facts.statement: Each premaxilla of Edgarosaurus contains either six or seven teeth.
facts.quote: Each premaxilla (front upper tooth bearing bone) contains either six or seven teeth.

facts.statement: Edgarosaurus had a short neck for a plesiosaur, consisting of a total of 26 vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neck of Edgarosaurus is short for a plesiosaur, containing a total of 26 vertebrae.

facts.statement: Compared to its close relatives, Edgarosaurus had a shorter and more robust face, a pineal opening on the top of the skull, and a slightly longer neck with 26 vertebrae.
facts.quote: Con respecto a sus parientes cercanos, los policotílidos, Edgarosaurus poseía un rostro más corto y robusto, una apertura pineal en la parte superior del cráneo y un cuello algo más alargado, con 26 vértebras.

facts.statement: Edgarosaurus was probably one of the most primitive polycotylids.
facts.quote: Edgarosaurus probablemente era uno de los policotílidos más primitivos.

facts.statement: The front ends of the mandible halves are fused to form a symphysis with six tooth pairs, which is a low number for a polycotylid.
facts.quote: The front ends of each half of the mandible are fused together to form a mandibular symphysis. There are six tooth pairs situated on the symphysis, a low number for a polycotylid.

facts.statement: Druckenmiller estimated that the neck and skull together comprised up to 45% of the animal's total length.
facts.quote: The neck and skull together were estimated by Druckenmiller to comprise up to 45% of the animal's length.

facts.statement: The lower arm bones of Edgarosaurus were very short and wide.
facts.quote: The lower arm bones of Edgarosaurus are very short and wide.

facts.statement: The forelimb digits of Edgarosaurus consist of seven, eleven, ten, and nine bones respectively for the first through fifth digits.
facts.quote: The first digit of its forelimb consists of seven bones, the second eleven, and the third ten, while the fourth and fifth bear nine.

rejected.statement: Edgarosaurus appears to have been part of an evolutionary radiation of short-necked plesiosaurs, the polycotylids, which were of reduced size and had a particularly hydrodynamic body shape.
rejected.quote: Parece que Edgarosaurus formó parte de una radiación evolutiva de plesiosaurios de cuello corto, los policotílidos, los cuales eran de dimensiones reducidas y con una forma corporal particularmente hidrodinámica.
